# Scenario X07 — Marketplace Acquisition Without Liquidity

**Domain:** Marketplace. **Situation:** health misdiagnosis by vanity metric.

## Context

A freelance-services marketplace ("GigPad") is 18 months old. The founder is presenting to
investors and to the board, citing strong growth: gross merchandise value doubled last
quarter and new seller signups are at an all-time high. The company is pitching a Series A
on "product-market fit achieved."

The data underneath: most listed gigs receive zero offers. Median time-to-first-hire for a
new buyer is 11 days. Supply (sellers) is growing faster than demand (buyers), so the
marketplace is acquiring supply with no matching. Monthly active buyers are roughly flat.
The company's churn of sellers who never got a single hire is high.

## Inputs available (imperfect)

- GMV doubled (but driven by a few large repeat sellers).
- Seller signups at all-time high (supply side only).
- Median time-to-first-hire 11 days; most gigs never get an offer.
- Buyer MAU flat.
- No cohort analysis of whether new sellers ever transact.

## Ask

You have one page to recommend what the founder should conclude about product-market fit and
what to do next. State your reasoning and the evidence you are relying on or missing.
